analysis.title: GS Hattori - GS ASIA What Happened?! (15 Oct 26)
key_insights: Japan and Korea both moved more than 2 standard deviations on 15 Oct. Japan's was the largest move since the start of the war and Korea's the largest since the July MOMO sell-off. Markets rebounded after previous drawdowns.
Across Asia the GS HT desk was 3.4x better to sell. Semis and hardware tech were 33% and 25% of executed flows. Short sell ratios were elevated in Japan, Korea and Taiwan.

Korea flow ended balanced on the desk because limited sell orders failed to complete in the relentless sell-off. In basket flow the desk saw macro capitulation across Japan and Korea, shorts added in Taiwan, and hedge funds turning to short selling in Semis/AI.
Desk buy interest is in China and India upside, where AI exposure is less concentrated, and in non-AI themes including Brazil, US/EU consumer, banks, healthcare and India.

Korea: foreigners net sold $2.8bn of equities, offset by domestic institutions plus retail. Retail was evenly skewed early and only came in to support the market as spot neared the lows of the day (Kospi2 -9.9%).
Taiwan: US$9.3bn net sold by foreigners, the most outflow in TWSE history. The second largest was 7/17 this year at about US$6bn.

Japan flow data is on a 1-week lag. Foreigners net sold $8bn of Japanese equities in the week ending Oct 2 (Nikkei +3%) versus $52bn average daily turnover. TSEMOTHR -3.2% implies little retail support in the sell-off.

The catalyst cited: Anthropic Q3 revenue of $16.8bn was a big miss versus a $5.4bn implied monthly run-rate for July, implying close to zero growth in August and September. This weighed on sentiment because frontier-model ARR growth is a key pillar of the AI investment thesis.

Funding stress at Coreweave and the neocloud ecosystem adds to concerns. The note's framing is that the core problem is capital access, since the data center boom is funded by debt and equity sales, which will have implications for capex.
Leverage: levered ETF AUM in Korea fell from 3.4% to 1.6% of free float cap, and is 0.7% in Taiwan and about 0.1% in Japan. The July sell-off was exacerbated by Korean leverage.

Net allocation to Asia equities is 30.2% (68th 1y percentile, 94th 5y percentile), so there was still length to sell, especially in Taiwan (7.2%, 79th 1y, 96th 5y). Japan 9.4% (66th/93rd), Korea 4.4% (47th/89th), China 7.2% (10th/20th).
Net allocation to global AI stocks is 26.1% of global single stock net MV, versus a peak of 31.7% in early June. That is the 49th percentile versus the past year and 83rd versus the past three years.

TSMC reported after the Taiwan close: EPS TWD 29.43 (+3.7% vs consensus 28.378), revenue TWD 1.49tr (+2.1% vs consensus 1.463tr). 4Q sales guide $52.3-54.3bn vs est $50.35bn, and 2026 capex still $60-64B. The author reads results as in line rather than a clean sweep, but the Japan/Korea reaction suggests it paused the tech de-risking.
Technicals: Kospi2 broke its 200DMA with RSI at 23 (oversold). NKY and TWSE are 5% and 15% above their 200DMAs with RSIs of 39.5 and 44.
Valuations: Taiwan multiples are well beyond historical highs, Japan P/B is at historical highs from a lower absolute level, and Korea P/B has corrected.

The note argues the bottleneck in AI is shifting from memory (Korea) to CPUs and custom ASICs, cooling, networking and multi-chip manufacturing (Taiwan and Japan), which could explain the divergence between Korean and Taiwanese flows. Asian markets are increasingly stock-picking rather than macro-trading environments, which could raise dispersion between markets.

Upcoming earnings: 70% of US index market cap reports by late October. About 90% of Topix reports over the next month (peaks Oct 31 and Nov 13). About 50% of TWSE reports Oct 29 to Nov 13. Samsung has reported and Hynix is expected Oct 28.

sector_views.rationale: Desk flows were dominated by selling in semis and hardware tech, and hedge funds turned to short selling in Semis/AI baskets.

earnings_insights: TSMC reported 15 Oct after the Taiwan close: EPS TWD 29.43 per share, +3.7% vs consensus est TWD 28.378 (reported). Revenue TWD 1.49tr, +2.1% vs consensus est TWD 1.463tr (reported).
TSMC 4Q sales guidance $52.3-54.3bn vs consensus est $50.35bn. 2026 capex guidance unchanged at $60-64B (no hike).

Earnings calendar: Hynix expected to report Oct 28 (Samsung already reported). About 90% of Topix reports over the next month, peaks Oct 31 and Nov 13. About 50% of TWSE reports Oct 29 to Nov 13. 70% of US index market cap reports by late October.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets rebounded after prior drawdowns, TSMC results and affirmed capex suggest hyperscalers have not trimmed deployment, Kospi2 is oversold at RSI 23, and leverage in Korea has fallen.
tension_points.bear_case: Net allocation to Asia equities is still 30.2% (94th 5y percentile), Taiwan valuations are beyond historical highs, and AI capital access is tightening after the Anthropic revenue miss and neocloud funding stress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further hit to AI capital access that implies lower capex, or no hike in TSMC capex limiting upside, as the note frames it.
